summary: Executed the incumbent's repair-and-regression action. Recipe: in a disposable copy of the middleware, change the safe-method branch to take the token from the client's cookie value and the state-changing branch to take it from the validated extracted token (both were previously copied from the stored placeholder value returned by the lookup); leave both backends and the public API unchanged. Then run a sixteen-check matrix: repeat-visit cookie stability, fresh-client and fresh-session constant requests, unknown-value control, legitimate victim and cross-client requests, form-field and cookie extraction variants, session-backed replay with session-cookie round trip, and single-use accept-then-replay-reject. Observed: every constant request rejected with the forbidden status in every configuration; no cookie ever collapsed to the constant; all legitimate flows accepted; single-use semantics preserved; two clients held different random tokens; upstream middleware suite fully green and the whole module built. Two unrelated timing-sensitive limiter suite failures were reproduced identically on pristine unmodified source and are pre-existing environment flakes, not caused by the change. The exported two-location source change applies cleanly to a pristine copy. These are local causal results with controls, not official harness results; official patch verification runs in a separate host-side harness and remains outstanding. Evidence strength: strong local support; limits: one runtime, in-process transport, no official verdict yet.
next_hint: The repair is complete locally and the regression matrix is green. The remaining step is procedural, not technical: hand the exported patch to the official host-side evaluation and record its verdict; no further local discriminating experiment is pending.
